newsitem.title: USA: Missouri corn seven pct planted, wheat improves.
newsitem.headline: Missouri corn seven pct planted, wheat improves.

text.p: Mild temperatures and dry weather allowed for rapid corn planting in the week ended Sunday, the state's Agricultural Statistics Service said.
"Particularly good corn planting progress was made in the extreme southern counties of the Bootheel, where reporters indicated as much as 60 to 80 percent (of the corn was) planted," the report said.
Statewide, the corn crop was seven percent planted, up from four percent for the five-year average.
Oats were 58 percent planted, compared with 54 percent last year and 50 percent for the five-year average.
A weekend storm system halted progress but an average of 4.8 days were rated suitable for fieldwork.
Winter wheat was rated one percent very poor, four percent poor, 25 fair, 55 percent good and 15 percent excellent.
Topsoil moisture was rated four percent short, 83 percent adequate and 13 percent surplus as of Friday.
Pasture and range conditions were rated one percent very poor, nine percent poor, 30 percent fair, 55 percent good and five percent excellent.
